items.title: William "Ba Ba" Ridgley Interview, 1959-06-02
items.q: I was still with Jeremy's family, I nursed the children, I did everything.

ctx.x: Were those all marches, or were some of the sort of jazz numbers too?

Marches, marches. That brass band at that time, they hadn't got to play no dance music. That's all they wanted to play a march. But he hadn't done pretty good. But I think they lost a good corner player that wouldn't go to the advantage when he died. They were doing fine. Well, they were the same way people that helped me, helped them. You see, I worked on a job, started when I was about 12 years old, and I worked there until I was around, I was about 18 years. And I did everything. I worked in the grocery, I was…

I was going to ask a little bit more about your family. If any other members of the family, any uncles or anyone played music? You say your father didn't play, didn't you? No. I had two brothers played.
